Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the call today — useful discussion. As promised, attaching our latency/throughput requirements (see attached) and a quick recap: our primary use case is real-time personalization for our mobile app. Key constraints:
- P50 latency target: <= 30ms end-to-end for text-generation features
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms
- Sustained throughput: ~500 requests/sec with diurnal spikes to ~1k/sec for 10–15 minutes

We don’t yet know exact model choice in production; likely a 7B–13B family with token lengths typically 32–128, sometimes up to 512 for certain flows. We need guidance on whether Redwood hosted API can meet these SLOs or whether we should plan for Dedicated capacity (or Private).

Can you confirm what performance profile we should expect from Hosted vs Dedicated for those numbers, and what the next steps are if Dedicated is recommended (pricing, timeline, any infra commitments)?

Thanks,
Amit Shah

Hi Amit —

Great to meet you and thanks for sending the doc. Quick recap and proposal based on the constraints you shared: 

1) Hosted API (Redwood Hosted)
- Pros: fastest path to production, no infra commitments, single API interface, built-in autoscaling and global edge routing.
- Cons: at p95 <=120ms for sustained 500 req/s it can be borderline depending on model size and traffic burst patterns. We have customers in the 100s req/s range with good p95s, but sustaining 500+ with p95 under 120ms usually benefits from Dedicated because you can reserve throughput and tune batching/instances.

2) Dedicated Capacity
- Pros: predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools, guaranteed capacity for spikes, ability to tune batching, KV caching and quantization profiles to hit tight p95 targets.
- Cons: commitment required (monthly reserved capacity) and small setup lead time (typically 2–4 weeks depending on region and instance type).

Recommendation: Given your p50/p95 targets and the 500–1k spikes, I think Dedicated is the safer option to start with — especially if you plan to run larger models (7B–13B) and need predictable latency during peaks. That said, we can run a short performance validation on Hosted to baseline expectations and then move to Dedicated if needed.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick SRE deep-dive with Dev to validate sample payloads and confirm sequence lengths / token usage (30–45 min)
- We run a Hosted validation (2–3 days) against a representative model and traffic profile
- If Hosted validation shows p95 >120ms at your target throughput, we provide a Dedicated sizing and pricing proposal and timeline (2–4 weeks to stand up)

Are you available early next week for the SRE deep-dive? If so, I’ll loop in Dev to coordinate. I’ll also have Dev include a short note on batching/latency tradeoffs so you have an idea of the expected delta between Hosted and Dedicated.

Best,

Hi Amit —

Following up with some technical color to help with the decision:

- Baseline assumptions I’d use for the Hosted validation: 13B model, 32–128 tokens typical, batch window 10–15ms, no heavy system-level preprocessing.
- With continuous batching at high QPS, Hosted can achieve good *throughput* but p95 is sensitive to tail queuing. Dedicated helps because we can:
  - Reserve enough GPU instances to keep effective batch sizes small (reduce queuing tail)
  - Use KV prefix caching for repeated prompts to shave tens of ms on hot flows
  - Apply quantization and kernel selection tuned to your model family for faster per-token throughput

Preliminary sizing (rough): to get p95 <=120ms at 500 sustained req/s for a 13B model, we’d likely recommend a Dedicated pool equivalent to ~8–12 x A100-class GPUs with tuned batching and autoscale headroom for 1k bursts. If you’re on 7B models you can probably achieve the same with ~4–6 GPUs.

Questions for you (will speed the validation/pricing):
- Do you have an internal P99 or P95 latency budget for the entire mobile flow (including network)?
- Do you expect payloads to be short (single prompt) or multi-turn/context heavy?
- Any regulatory constraints (e.g., need for VPC, customer-managed keys)?

I’m available for the SRE deep-dive Tue/Wed next week (PST). If you can share a small sample of typical request payloads (anonymized) that’ll help us craft the Hosted validation test.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
